Done. I wrote and ran a complete, self-contained analysis.py and produced all four artifacts. Both locked decisions are implemented: the τ₀ offset is INCLUDED, and tail_asymmetry = post-peak energy / pre-peak energy on the output waveform (documented in a comment).

MODEL (physics-informed lossy transmission line)
H(ω; line) = exp(-jωτ₀) · exp(-γ(ω; line)·L),  γ = α + jβ
• Phase: β(ω; line) = D(ω; line)·ω·√(L·C). D(ω; line) = D₀(ω) + [linear correction in (roughness, Rdc, width)]. D₀ is a smooth global dispersion factor (~0.993–1.005); the correction removes most of the ~0.17% per-line spread. τ₀ is a global pure-delay offset fit to MINIMISE THE TOTAL PHASE RESIDUAL of the full model → τ₀ = 0.4597 ns.
• Loss: α(ω; line) = (Rdc·S(ω; W, rough)/2)·√(C/L) + (G/2)·√(L/C), with S(ω; W, rough) = A(ω)·W^0.5652·rough^0.0190 and A(ω) a smooth √ω skin factor fitted from the data.
• Phase_rad is computed directly (monotonic, no 2π jumps). group_delay_s = -d(phase_rad)/d(ω) computed NUMERICALLY (np.gradient) from the SAME reported phase array, so the two columns match to floating-point precision.
• Waveforms: 2049-pt positive grid → full 4096-pt H via conjugate symmetry; output = IFFT(FFT(input)·H). Real output.

VERIFICATION (the model reproduces the 8 calibration lines):
• mean|Δphase| = 0.52 rad (per line 0.06–1.22 rad); max ~2.4 rad only at 62.5 GHz.
• mean|Δmagnitude| = 0.33 dB (per line 0.11–0.63 dB).
• mean|Δgroup_delay| = 5–7.5 ps (on 5–11 ns delays, ~0.1% relative).
• target_transfer.csv: phase strictly monotonic (max step 2.17 rad < 2π); group_delay vs -d(phase)/d(ω) recomputed from the CSV agrees to 3.4e-21 s. No NaN/Inf in any file.

PREDICTED TARGETS (L, Rdc, mag@62.5GHz, phase@62.5GHz, gd@DC):
• target_0 (1.10 m, 0.154): -8.4 dB, -2100 rad, 5.41 ns
• target_1 (1.72 m, 0.274): -17.3 dB, -3226 rad, 8.31 ns
• target_2 (2.35 m, 0.389): -25.8 dB, -4389 rad, 11.31 ns

PULSE METRICS (input FWHM 0.208 ns for all):
• target_0: out FWHM 0.216 ns (ratio 1.04), peak delay 5.35 ns, peak t 9.86 ns, energy 0.863, tail_asym 1.374
• target_1: out FWHM 0.224 ns (ratio 1.08), peak delay 8.22 ns, peak t 12.73 ns, energy 0.742, tail_asym 1.345
• target_2: out FWHM 0.232 ns (ratio 1.12), peak delay 11.19 ns, peak t 15.70 ns, energy 0.646, tail_asym 1.317
The waveforms are clean, slightly attenuated/broadened pulses whose peak delay equals the group delay — physically correct.

DIAGNOSTIC: the simple telegrapher equation γ²=(R+jωL)(G+jωC) does NOT close with the given L,C (mean fractional real-part mismatch ~1.4%), which is why I used the empirical D(ω) dispersion model rather than the raw telegrapher form.
